2608.13173.title: SkillShapley: Boundary-Adaptive Shapley Valuation for Skill Step Attribution in LLM Agents
2608.13173.paper_summary: Agent skills are crucial external instructions that enable language agents to execute long procedural tasks such as coding or document processing. Existing agent skills are primarily created through human manual crafting or agent execution traces, with limited understanding of how each step contributes to overall skill performance on specific tasks; i.e., there remains an open problem in quantifying the contribution of individual steps within an agent skill. To address this issue, we first model skill-step attribution as a Shapley value-based contribution estimation problem, and then propose SkillShapley, a step-level attribution framework for agent skills. Notably, SkillShapley operates in two phases, motivated by key empirical insights, i.e., discretized benchmark rewards that create sharp performance cliffs, and step interactions that are largely additive rather than synergistic. Specifically, it first identifies informative coalitional regions, and then adaptively samples new coalitions that can yield reusable marginal evidence. Experiments on skills from the widely adopted SkillsBench demonstrate that our SkillShapley can effectively and efficiently identify high- or low-value skill steps, providing several key takeaways for agent skill creation.
2608.13173.paper_summary_zh: 代理技能是關鍵的外部指令，使語言代理能夠執行長期的程序性任務，例如編碼或文檔處理。現有的代理技能主要通過人為手動製作或代理執行痕跡創建，對於每一步如何貢獻於特定任務的整體技能表現的理解有限；也就是說，在量化代理技能中各個步驟的貢獻方面仍然存在一個未解決的問題。為了解決這個問題，我們首先將技能步驟歸因建模為基於Shapley值的貢獻估計問題，然後提出SkillShapley，一個針對代理技能的步驟級歸因框架。值得注意的是，SkillShapley在兩個階段運作，這受到關鍵實證見解的驅動，即離散化的基準獎勵創造了明顯的性能懸崖，以及步驟之間的互動主要是加法而非協同的。具體而言，它首先識別信息豐富的聯合區域，然後自適應地抽樣可以產生可重用邊際證據的新聯合體。在廣泛採用的SkillsBench上的技能實驗表明，我們的SkillShapley可以有效且高效地識別高價值或低價值的技能步驟，為代理技能的創建提供幾個關鍵的啟示。
